These events → Disaster Management Act 2005: NDMA (National Disaster Management Authority) — PM as chairman; SDMA (State DMA); DDMA (District); NDRF (National Disaster Response Force). Health angle: National Disaster Response Plan — pre-positioning medical teams, emergency drugs, blood; HEMS (Health Emergency Management Standard). Odisha model: zero casualty target (cyclone FANI 2019 — 10 million evacuated, 64 deaths)।

question: भारत में 'Tobacco Cessation' सेवाओं का विकास — iCTC, mCessation, NHM Clinic:

options.text: India में tobacco cessation services 2020 में शुरू हुईं

iCTC (Integrated Counselling and Testing Centres से अलग — tobacco iCTC): NHP + WHO collaboration; NTCP (2007) में cessation centers; National Tobacco Quitline (1800-11-2356); mCessation (WHO-India, 2016) — mobile-based behavior change; National Cancer Helpline (1800-180-4141)
India में tobacco cessation में ASHA की कोई भूमिका नहीं है
Tobacco cessation medicines India में available नहीं हैं

explanation: Tobacco Cessation India: (1) NTCP (National Tobacco Control Programme, 2007-08): District Tobacco Control Cells; cessation centers at District Hospitals; awareness campaigns; (2) National Tobacco Quitline: 1800-11-2356 (free); behavioural counselling; (3) mCessation: WHO-India project (2016) — mobile-based SMS reminders + counselling; reached millions; (4) Tobacco Cessation Centres (TCC) at medical colleges and district hospitals; NRT (Nicotine Replacement Therapy): patches, gum; Bupropion, Varenicline — prescription medicines; (5) ASHA: IEC on tobacco hazards, SHG discussions, referral. FCTC Article 14 (demand reduction — cessation) — India obligation. GATS (Global Adult Tobacco Survey) India: tobacco use 34.6% (2009-10) → 28.6% (2016-17)।

question: भारत में 'मिड-डे मील' और 'पोषण' — Supreme Court orders से PM POSHAN तक:

options.text: Mid-Day Meal Programme 1990 में शुरू हुआ

MDM State schemes 1960s में; National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education (NP-NSPE, 1995) — central; PUCL v Union of India (2001) SC orders — mandatory cooked meal; 2001-04 में SC active monitoring; PM POSHAN (2021) = MDM rename + expansion to pre-primary
SC ने Mid-Day Meal को unconstitutional माना
Mid-Day Meal केवल government schools में है

explanation: Mid-Day Meal history: (1) State schemes (Tamil Nadu 1960s — Jayalalithaa MDM famous), MP, Kerala; (2) National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education (NP-NSPE, 1995) — central programme; dry rations; (3) PUCL v Union of India (2001): SC PIL — Right to Food case; Court ordered: (a) cooked meal (not dry ration) within 6 months; (b) minimum nutritional content; (4) SC monitoring: 2004 directions — 450 calories + 12g protein for primary, higher for upper primary; (5) National Food Security Act 2013: MDM as legal entitlement; (6) PM POSHAN (Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman, 2021): renamed + expanded to pre-primary (Bal Vatikas at Anganwadi). Coverage: 11.8 crore children; 10 lakh+ schools. Nutritional impact: micronutrient-fortified rice — recent addition।

question: भारत में 'PCPNDT Act' enforcement और 'Missing Women' phenomenon — Amartya Sen से NFHS-5 तक:

options.text: India में sex ratio consistently improving रही है

Amartya Sen (1990) ने 'Missing Women' phenomenon — South Asia, China में sex-selective practices से करोड़ों women demographically absent; PC-PNDT (1994, 2003) enforcement weak; CSR 2011: 919 (lowest since independence); BBBP (2015) — 640 districts; NFHS-5 CSR: 929 — marginal improvement
India में sex ratio problem नहीं है
BBBP केवल education के लिए है

explanation: Missing Women: Amartya Sen (1990, NYRB): 'More Than 100 Million Women Are Missing' — excess female mortality and sex-selective practices in South Asia, China, Sub-Saharan Africa. India: (1) CSR (Child Sex Ratio 0-6 years): 1961: 976 → 1991: 945 → 2001: 927 → 2011: 919 per 1000 boys — secular decline despite PC-PNDT; (2) Ultrasound machines proliferation (1980s) made prenatal sex determination easy; (3) PC-PNDT enforcement: Form F (ultrasound record) — manipulation common; SC vigilance; but only 500-600 convictions nationally; (4) BBBP (Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, 2015) — 640 Aspirational Districts → CSR improvement; (5) NFHS-5: CSR 929 — some recovery. Bihar, UP — higher CSR than Punjab-Haryana (historically low).

question: भारत में 'National Nutrition Policy' (1993) और 'NNM' (National Nutrition Mission/POSHAN) — nutrition governance का विकास:

options.text: India में कोई formal nutrition policy नहीं है

NNP (1993) — multi-sectoral; NPNHP (2000); National Nutrition Mission renamed POSHAN Abhiyaan (2018) — district-level targets (stunting, wasting, anaemia); Real-time Monitoring (RTM); Poshan Maah (September); POSHAN 2.0 (2021) — Saksham Anganwadi integration
POSHAN Abhiyaan का लक्ष्य केवल anaemia है
India में stunting बढ़ रहा है

explanation: Nutrition policy India: (1) National Nutrition Policy (NNP, 1993): multi-sectoral approach — food production, distribution, ICDS, education; (2) National Plan of Action for Nutrition (NPAN, 1995); (3) NPNHP (2000); (4) POSHAN Abhiyaan (PM's Overarching Scheme for Holistic Nourishment, March 2018): ₹9046 crore; targets — reduce stunting by 2% /year, wasting 2%/year, LBW 2%/year, anaemia 3%/year; ICDS + PMMVY + MDMS + Swachh Bharat convergence; Real-Time Monitoring (RTM) on POSHAN Tracker (mobile app); Poshan Maah (September) — awareness; (5) POSHAN 2.0 (2021): Umbrella — Saksham Anganwadi + POSHAN 2.0; nutrition sensitive interventions. Results: NFHS-5 stunting 35.5% vs NFHS-4 38.4%; wasting NFHS-5: 19.3% (slight rise from 21%); underweight: 32.1% (slight improvement)।

question: भारत में 'ASHA Didi' से 'ASHA Sahyogini' — ASHA worker की बदलती भूमिका और incentive structure:

options.text: ASHA को fixed salary मिलती है

ASHA 2005 से performance-based incentive (task-based payments — delivery escort ₹600, child immunization ₹100, TB case ₹500 etc.); minimum ₹2000/month guarantee (कुछ states); 2023 में केंद्र ने ₹2000 guaranteed और incentives revised; ASHAs = world's largest CHW force (10.5 lakh)
ASHAs केवल vaccination करती हैं
ASHA का कोई incentive structure नहीं है

explanation: ASHA incentive structure: Originally (2005): task-based payments only — no fixed salary. Incentives: (1) JSY escort: ₹600 (rural), ₹200 (urban); (2) Full immunization child: ₹100; (3) New TB case detection: ₹500 + ₹500 on treatment completion; (4) Home delivery referral, ANC registration, Family planning, Deworming, Vitamin A. Average earnings: ₹2000-4000/month (variable). Evolution: (1) Many states supplement (Bihar: ₹1000 state top-up; UP, Karnataka — similar); (2) 2023: Central government enhanced — minimum ₹2000 guaranteed + enhanced incentives (TB: ₹1000, delivery: ₹800). National ASHA Sammelan — annual; ASHA Training (ASHA in-service training days). Scale: 10.5 lakh ASHAs in 2024 — world's largest CHW force (WHO recognition)।

question: भारत में 'Maternal Mortality' decline — 1990 से 2020 तक क्या structural factors ने MMR कम किया?

options.text: India में MMR decline केवल JSY की वजह से हुई

Institutional delivery increase (JSY, JSSK), skilled birth attendance, SNCU नवजात care, anemia treatment (IFA supplementation), EmOC (Emergency Obstetric Care) capacity, Blood bank access, ASHA accompaniment — multi-factorial; SRS MMR: 2004-06: 254 → 2018-20: 97
India ने SDG MMR target पहले ही achieve कर लिया है
MMR India में बढ़ रहा है

explanation: India MMR Decline (SRS): 2004-06: 254 → 2010-12: 178 → 2014-16: 130 → 2016-18: 113 → 2018-20: 97 per 1,00,000 live births. Multi-factorial contributors: (1) JSY (2005): institutional delivery incentive — cash; (2) JSSK (2011): zero-expense delivery; (3) ASHA mobilization: ANC registration, facility delivery; (4) Anemia control: IFA supplementation (900 tablets scheme); (5) Emergency Obstetric Care (EmOC): blood banks, magnesium sulphate for eclampsia; (6) SNCU (neonatal care); (7) Skilled Birth Attendance training (SBA trainings for ANMs); (8) PMSMA (Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan, 2016) — fixed-day ANC at PHC. State variation: Kerala MMR (19), Tamil Nadu (58) vs. UP (167), Assam (195). SDG target: <70 by 2030 — NHP 2017 target: <100 (achieved!)।

question: भारत में 'Social Determinants of Health' — CSDH (2008) और India की नीतिगत response:

options.text: India में social determinants को health policy में शामिल नहीं किया गया है

WHO Commission on Social Determinants of Health (Marmot, 2008) ने 'Closing the Gap in a Generation' दिया; India में: NHP 2017 ने SDH को explicitly include किया; Aspirational Districts Programme में multi-sectoral convergence; HWC में WASH, nutrition, mental health link; NITI Aayog SDG India Index
SDH theory केवल academic concept है — India policy में नहीं
India में poverty और health का कोई documented link नहीं है

explanation: CSDH (Commission on Social Determinants of Health) 2008 (WHO, chaired by Michael Marmot): 'Closing the Gap in a Generation — Health Equity through Action on SDH.' Key message: daily living conditions + structural drivers = inequitable health outcomes. India policy response: (1) NHP 2017 — SDH explicitly mentioned: 'Address social, environmental and economic determinants of health'; (2) Ayushman Bharat HWC — 12 service packages include WASH, nutrition counselling; (3) Aspirational Districts Programme (NITI Aayog, 2018) — 5 domains (health, education, agriculture, financial inclusion, infrastructure) — multi-sectoral; (4) POSHAN Abhiyaan — nutrition + sanitation + health convergence; (5) Swachh Bharat Mission + JJM + ICDS = SDH interventions. NITI Aayog SDG Index: health SDG tracked alongside education, income, gender equality।

question: भारत में 'NIPAH Virus' का इतिहास और One Health approach की जरूरत:

options.text: Nipah केवल Bangladesh की बीमारी है

India में Nipah: Siliguri (2001, hospital amplification), Nadia WB (2007), Kozhikode Kerala (2018, 17 deaths), 2023, 2024 outbreaks; Pteropus bats = reservoir; Kerala containment model (DISHA, contact tracing); ICMR + NCDC + WHO collaboration; One Health: bat ecology + agriculture + human health
Nipah का मनुष्यों से मनुष्यों में transmission नहीं होता
Nipah का कोई vaccine available है

explanation: Nipah Virus India history: (1) Siliguri (2001): 66 cases, 45 deaths (CFR 68%); hospital amplification; date palm sap suspected; (2) Nadia, WB (2007): 5 cases, 4 deaths; (3) Kozhikode-Malappuram, Kerala (2018): 19 cases, 17 deaths (CFR 89%); index case Muhammed Sabith — bat contact; DISHA helpline + ring containment; (4) Ernakulam 2023: 2 deaths, 700 contacts; (5) Kozhikode 2024: contained. Kerala Model: DISHA call centre, Geographic ring containment, rapid sample testing (NIV Pune), contact tracing — zero healthcare worker death (PPE). One Health framework: bat roosting (Pteropus medius) + fruit orchards + humans = NiV emergence. ICMR surveillance: 13 states with bat sampling। NiV = BSL-4 pathogen — no approved vaccine (monoclonal antibody m102.4 compassionate use)।

question: भारत में 'Domestic Violence Act 2005' और महिलाओं के mental और physical health पर इसका प्रभाव:

options.text: Domestic Violence Act केवल legal rights के लिए है — health से कोई संबंध नहीं

Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005: physical, sexual, emotional, verbal, economic violence को परिभाषित किया; Protection Officer + Medical Examination mandate; NFHS-5: 29.3% महिलाएं domestic violence experience; DV और depression, anxiety, PTSD, nutritional neglect, pregnancy complications link
PWDVA 2005 में medical evidence का कोई उल्लेख नहीं है
India में domestic violence आम नहीं है

explanation: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act (PWDVA) 2005: India का पहला comprehensive civil law for domestic violence (IPC 498A — criminal, already existed). Definitions: physical, sexual, verbal/emotional, economic violence + controlling behavior। Health provisions: (1) Medical examination of aggrieved person — mandatory Protocol; (2) Protection Officer duties include medical aid referral; (3) One-Stop Centres (Sakhi, 2015) — co-located with medical facility. Health impacts documented: (1) NFHS-5: 29.3% married women experienced spousal violence; (2) Mental health: depression, PTSD, anxiety (OR 2-4x); (3) Nutritional outcomes: abused women 2x more likely to be anaemic; (4) Reproductive health: pregnancy complications, miscarriage; (5) Child health: children witnessing DV → developmental delays. WHO report (2013): violence against women = global public health problem।

question: भारत में 'NLEP' (National Leprosy Eradication Programme) और MDT (Multi Drug Therapy) — 1983 से 2005 उन्मूलन तक:

options.text: India में leprosy 1947 में समाप्त हो गई थी

NLEP (1983) ने WHO-recommended MDT (Dapsone+Rifampicin+Clofazimine) अपनाई; 1991 में WHO ने elimination target (<1/10,000) दिया; India 2005 में elimination achieved; पर sub-national hotspots बचे; Lepers Act 1898 निरसित (2016); stigma reduction = अधूरा काम
MDT का India में कोई प्रभाव नहीं हुआ
India में leprosy cases 2023 में बढ़ रहे हैं

explanation: NLEP & MDT history: (1) Leprosy prevalence India 1951: 38/10,000 → 1981: 57/10,000 (actually increased — better detection); (2) NLEP (1983): free MDT — WHO recommended 2-drug (PB: dapsone+rifampicin) and 3-drug (MB: +clofazimine) — 6/12 months; (3) WHO Global Leprosy Elimination target (1991): <1 case per 10,000 population — India achieved 2005; (4) Post-elimination: hotspots remain — Chhattisgarh, Bihar, UP, Odisha; new cases ~1 lakh/year (still significant); (5) Lepers Act 1898: Repealing & Amending Act 2016; Personal Laws Amendment 2019 (leprosy no longer grounds for divorce). WHO Global Leprosy Strategy 2021-2030 — zero leprosy. India's sub-elimination states goal। Early detection + MDT = cure; grade 2 disability prevention।

question: भारत में 'WHO Essential Medicines List' और 'National EML' का ऐतिहासिक विकास:

options.text: India में कोई National EML नहीं है

WHO EML (1977, पहली list — 205 drugs); HAHO (Health Action by People) आंदोलन + India ने Sokhey Committee विचार → NLEM 1996 → NLEM 2003 → 2011 → NLEM 2022 (384 medicines); DPCO 2013 NLEM पर based; free medicine initiatives (Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu) NLEM से guide होती हैं
WHO EML 2000 में शुरू हुई
NLEM में केवल antibiotics शामिल हैं

explanation: WHO EML history: First Essential Medicines List (1977): 205 medicines — concept: 'medicines that satisfy priority health care needs of population'; cost-effective; based on prevalence, safety, efficacy, comparative cost. India NLEM: (1) 1996 — first NLEM; (2) 2003 update; (3) NLEM 2011 — 348 medicines (basis for DPCO 2013); (4) NLEM 2022 — 384 medicines (additions: anti-cancer drugs, mifepristone, insulin analogues, bedaquiline for MDR-TB, direct-acting antivirals for Hepatitis C). Uses: (1) DPCO 2013 — price control for NLEM drugs; (2) Free medicine schemes (Rajasthan, TN); (3) PM-JAY reimbursement; (4) CGHS, ESI formularies. WHO 34th EML (2024) — now 502 medicines. Critiques: some expensive drugs missing; WHO process transparent, India process less so।

question: भारत में 'Mental Healthcare Act 2017' का 1987 Act से क्या revolutionary shift था?

options.text: Mental Healthcare Act 2017 ने mental health को criminal domain में रखा

Rights-based approach: self-harm decriminalized (IPC 309 exception), right to informed consent + refuse treatment, right to confidentiality, prohibition of outdated treatments (ECST without consent), right to make 'advance directives', nominated representative system; shift from 'patient' to 'person with psychosocial disability'
MHA 2017 ने asylums को legal status दिया
MHA 2017 में NIMHANS का कोई उल्लेख नहीं है

explanation: Mental Healthcare Act 2017 vs Mental Health Act 1987: 1987 — institutionalization focus, patient's rights minimal, magistrate-based admission. 2017 — rights-based paradigm (CRPD-aligned): (1) Right to access mental health care; (2) Right to informed consent and refuse treatment (except imminent danger); (3) Advance Directive: person can pre-specify treatment preferences; (4) Nominated Representative; (5) Right to confidentiality; (6) Prohibition: Electric Convulsive Therapy (ECST) without consent/anaesthesia; aversive therapy; sterilization without consent; (7) Decriminalization of suicide attempt — IPC 309 remains but MHA 2017 Sec 115 — 'presumed to have mental illness' — rehabilitation not punishment; (8) Shift: UNCRPD language — 'psychosocial disability'; (9) Mental Health Review Board (MHRB) in districts — quasi-judicial oversight। Implementation challenges: MHRB not fully established in all states。

question: भारत में 'प्रजनन और बाल स्वास्थ्य सर्वेक्षण' — NFHS के पाँच चरणों का तुलनात्मक analysis:

options.text: NFHS केवल population count के लिए है

NFHS (IIPS, DHS programme): NFHS-1 (1992-93), NFHS-2 (1998-99), NFHS-3 (2005-06), NFHS-4 (2015-16), NFHS-5 (2019-21); प्रत्येक में indicators expand हुए; NFHS-5 ने pहली बार district-level data दिया (707 districts); HTN, diabetes screening; CSR, MMR proxies; NHM monitoring का backbone
India में NFHS केवल एक बार हुआ है
NFHS में immunization data नहीं होती

explanation: NFHS (National Family Health Survey): DHS Programme (USAID) के technical framework पर; conducted by IIPS (International Institute for Population Sciences, Mumbai). NFHS timeline: (1) NFHS-1 (1992-93): baseline; (2) NFHS-2 (1998-99); (3) NFHS-3 (2005-06); (4) NFHS-4 (2015-16): district-level for first time; (5) NFHS-5 (2019-21): 707 districts; new additions — Hypertension, Diabetes screening, anaemia (Haemoglobinometer), alcohol use, mental health (PHQ-9 in some states). Key indicators tracked: TFR, IMR, MMR proxy, U5MR, institutional delivery, stunting/wasting/underweight, anaemia, breastfeeding, immunization coverage, spousal violence, women's empowerment. Policy use: NHP 2017, SDG tracking, POSHAN monitoring।

question: भारत में 'ayushman Bharat Digital Mission' (ABDM) और Health data governance:

options.text: ABDM एक private company चलाती है

ABDM (2021, National Health Authority): ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account — 14-digit ID), Health Records (DigiLocker), HRPR (Healthcare Provider Registry), UHI (Unified Health Interface); Data protection: Personal Data Protection Bill (2023) के आने से पहले gap; digital health equity concern
ABDM में privacy का कोई concern नहीं है
ABHA enrollment mandatory है

explanation: Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM, 2021): National Health Authority (NHA) implements. Components: (1) ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account, 14-digit) — unique health identifier; 54+ crore enrolled (2024); (2) Health Locker — patient controls their health records; (3) HRPR (Health Facility & Professional Registry) — hospital, doctor registration; (4) UHI (Unified Health Interface) — like UPI for health payments/appointments. Data governance: Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 — data privacy framework (not specifically health); HDMP (Health Data Management Policy, 2020) — draft for health data. Challenges: (1) Urban-rural digital divide; (2) Private sector opt-in; (3) Interoperability across systems; (4) Informed consent for data sharing. International comparison: UK NHS Data (care.data controversy); Estonia e-Health (successful model). ABDM = India's aspirational model — implementation gaps remain।

question: 'McKeown Thesis' (1976) और उसकी भारतीय संदर्भ में प्रासंगिकता:

options.text: McKeown ने कहा कि vaccines ने mortality decline किया

Thomas McKeown (1976): England में TB decline medicine/vaccines से पहले — nutrition improvement + living conditions से; 'Biomedical model की सीमाएं'; India में relevance: 1990s food security improvement ने health outcomes को antibiotics से पहले impact किया; पर India में biomedical interventions (DOTS, JSY, ORS) भी critical
McKeown Thesis ने antibiotics की महत्व को overstate किया
McKeown की Theory India में fully applicable है

explanation: McKeown Thesis (Thomas McKeown, 'The Modern Rise of Population,' 1976): England में TB mortality 1850 से decline — streptomycin (1947) से decades पहले; pasteurization, BCG, notification से पहले। McKeown's conclusion: 'nutritional improvement → immune function → disease resistance' = primary driver. Debate: Fogel (nutritional) agreed; Szreter (sanitation) disagreed; McKeown = oversimplified. India relevance: (1) Green Revolution (1965-68) → food security → nutrition → child mortality some decline; (2) BUT India: ORS (oral rehydration), vaccines, DOTS = clear causal link — biomedical interventions worked; (3) Bihar: food security poor + biomedical (ORS) still reduced child diarrheal mortality; Conclusion: India = both nutrition AND biomedical interventions needed — McKeown + Contra-McKeown both valid for different contexts।

question: भारत में 'Accreditation' और quality assurance — NABH, LaQshya, Manyata का ऐतिहासिक विकास:

options.text: India में hospital quality certification 1947 से है

NABH (National Accreditation Board for Hospitals, 2005, QCI); public hospital NABH — Kayakalp (2015, ODF-cleanliness), LaQshya (2017, Labour Room Quality), Manyata (private facility RMNCH quality); MOHFW Quality Cell; COVID-19 ने PPE, IPC protocols को quality framework में add किया
NABH केवल private hospitals के लिए है
LaQshya केवल OPD quality के लिए है

explanation: Hospital Quality India: (1) NABH (National Accreditation Board for Hospitals & Healthcare Providers, 2005): Quality Council of India (QCI) under DPIIT; voluntary accreditation — 300+ standards; 700+ hospitals accredited (2024); international recognition — ISQua accredited. (2) Public facility quality: Kayakalp (2015) — cleanliness + sanitation + infection control; Cash award ₹50 lakh for district hospital; LaQshya (2017, Quality Improvement in Labour Room & OT) — maternal care quality; Manyata (private facility RMNCH quality program — JHPIEGO). (3) NHM Quality Assurance framework: Divisional/Block level QA Committees; Citizen Charter; Patient Satisfaction Survey। COVID additions: IPC (Infection Prevention & Control) standards strengthened; PPE procurement quality control (BIS). (4) HWC CPHC quality: Standard Treatment Workflows (STW) — clinical protocols for CHO।

question: भारत में 'Right to Information Act 2005' का सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य में कैसे उपयोग हुआ?

options.text: RTI का स्वास्थ्य क्षेत्र से कोई संबंध नहीं है

RTI (2005) ने drug purchase irregularities, drug quality failures, vacancies, fund utilization को नागरिकों के सामने रखा; SATHI (Pune), Jan Swasthya Abhiyan ने health RTI activist role निभाया; Community Score Cards और Social Audit इसी transparency framework में; MOHFW RTI cell
RTI से सरकारी अस्पताल बंद होने का खतरा है
RTI केवल financial information के लिए है

explanation: RTI Act 2005 and Public Health India: RTI के तहत: (1) Drug procurement: NHM drug purchase irregularities exposed (MP, Bihar); (2) HMIS data quality questioned; (3) PHC doctor vacancies and absenteeism revealed; (4) Fund utilization: NHM unspent balance — CAG + RTI. Civil society organizations: SATHI (Support for Advocacy and Training to Health Initiatives, Pune) — health RTI campaign; Jan Swasthya Abhiyan (JSA) — RTI for public health accountability. Community tools linked with RTI: Social Audit (MGNREGS model → NHM social audit); Jan Sunwai (public hearings); Community Score Cards. MOHFW RTI Cell: पहले RTI officer in ministry. Supreme Court (PUCL v UOI 2001 + Nandini Sundar v State of Chhattisgarh) — RTI as extension of Art.19 (speech) and 21 (life). RTI transparency = accountability mechanism in health.

question: भारत में 'CGHS' (Central Government Health Scheme) का इतिहास और UHC में इसकी सीमाएं:

options.text: CGHS सभी भारतीय नागरिकों के लिए है

CGHS 1954 में Delhi में शुरू; current + retired central govt employees + MPs + judges + freedom fighters; ₹1.1 crore+ beneficiaries (2024); 85 cities में Wellness Centres; cashless empanelled hospitals; limitations: urban-centric, 50 crore आबादी को नहीं cover; ESIC, Defence, Railway — अलग schemes
CGHS ने PM-JAY को replace किया
CGHS में केवल allopathy available है

explanation: CGHS (Central Government Health Scheme): Established 1954, Delhi — central govt employees ka health scheme. Coverage: (1) Current + retired central govt employees; (2) MPs, ex-MPs; (3) Judges (SC, High Courts); (4) Freedom fighters; (5) Dependents. Cities: 85 cities में CGHS Wellness Centres। Services: OPD, specialist referral, diagnostic, cashless empanelled hospitals (govt + private). Systems: AYUSH also available (Ayurveda, Homeopathy Wellness Centres). Budget: ₹4,000+ crore/year. Beneficiaries: 11+ lakh families (~35 lakh individuals). Limitations: (1) Only central government — state govt employees not covered (state schemes: TNHS, Rajasthan GSS, etc.); (2) Urban-centric — 85 cities; (3) India's 140 crore population में only 35 lakh direct beneficiaries; (4) Quality and timely care concerns at govt hospitals. Other schemes: ESIC (organised sector workers), Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme (ECHS), Railway Health Scheme.
